newsitem.title: ITALY: SWIMMING-POLL SWIMS TO WORLD CUP DOUBLE.
newsitem.headline: SWIMMING-POLL SWIMS TO WORLD CUP DOUBLE.

text.p: Olympic champion Claudia Poll swam to a double success on the first day of a World Cup short-course meeting on Tuesday.
The Costa Rican won the 200 metres freestyle in one minute 58.79 and had the satisfaction of seeing China's Olympics 100 metres freestyle gold medallist Jingyi Le trail in third in 2:00.64.
Poll, who took five months off after the Atlanta Olympics, also won the 800 metres freestyle in 8:35.41, 0.06 of a second clear of Kirsten Vlieghuis of the Netherlands.
Jingyi, returning to World Cup competition after a break, fared better in the 50 metres freestyle but still had to be content with second place behind Leah Martindale of Barbados.

Martindale, who finished 0.05 ahead in 25.26, said she eased off training after a meeting in Glasgow late last month. "I've been resting a bit more since Scotland and it's helping," she said. "I was happy with that swim."
Antje Buschschulte, fresh from five medals in Gelsenkirchen, Germany earlier this week, won the 50 metres backstroke in a personal best 27.94 and then took the 200 backstroke in 2:09.25.
"This is not as important for me as the long-course season, but nevertheless I am a bit prepared," the German said.
